entrypoints.summary: POST /unzip accepts a multipart zipfile, writes its supplied bytes to a SHA-256-derived /tmp path, then runs unzip with the -: option.
POST /un7z accepts a multipart zipfile and invokes 7z extraction before re-archiving the extraction directory into the HTTP response.

affected_components.role: Accepts ZIP uploads, derives SHA-256 temporary names, invokes unzip or 7z, re-archives the resulting directory, and returns it.
Constructs traversed .z01/.z02 entries and a multidisk archive whose second component is a symlink to /flag.

causal_paths.kind: Multidisk component to returned archive content

negative_controls: No execution transcript or negative-control response is present in the bundle.
observability.positive_marker: The exploit reads and prints a decoded entry from the returned ZIP, intended to contain the flag-derived data.

preconditions: The service exposes the HTTP /unzip and /un7z endpoints.
The runtime has p7zip, unzip, and zip installed and the process can read /flag.
The archive utilities retain the behavior described by the organizer writeup.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: ZIP whose entries use ../<sha>.z01 and ../<sha>.z02 names; the .z02 entry has symlink mode and /flag as its target.
trigger_steps.summary: POST a crafted setup ZIP to /unzip to create traversed, predictably named .z01 and .z02 components; the latter is a symlink to /flag.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Final disk containing matching central-directory metadata for a multipart archive.
trigger_steps.summary: POST the matching final multidisk .zip component to /un7z and parse its returned ZIP response.

capabilities.concept: Archive path traversal and symlink placement
Read container-local file through re-archived extraction output

relation_candidates.dst: Archive path traversal and symlink placement
relation_candidates.rationale: The upload reaches /unzip, whose -: invocation is documented as allowing traversed entry paths and unsafe symlinks.
Traversal places the predictable .z01/.z02/.zip components where 7z will locate them, with .z02 represented as a symlink to /flag.
relation_candidates.src: Archive path traversal and symlink placement

relation_candidates.dst: Read container-local file through re-archived extraction output
relation_candidates.rationale: The writeup explains that 7z consumes the symlinked second disk as archive data, after which the service zips and returns the created file.
The supplied exploit posts both stages and reads a returned ZIP entry; the runtime image places the flag in /flag.
relation_candidates.src: Read container-local file through re-archived extraction output

relation_candidates.rationale: The writeup's proposed defenses are to eliminate traversal and symlink-following extraction, reject multidisk/links, isolate tools, and avoid cross-tool reprocessing.
relation_candidates.src: Archive path traversal and symlink placement

impact.affected_asset: The container-local flag file at /flag; the runtime image writes a flag there.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote HTTP client can cause content from /flag, reached through a symlinked multidisk archive segment, to be included in a response archive.
impact.security_effect: Arbitrary local file content disclosure through the returned ZIP archive.

causal_trace.summary: The attacker controls the uploaded ZIP bytes accepted by both extraction endpoints; the service derives the temporary base filename from SHA-256 of those same bytes.

The /unzip path runs unzip with -:, which the organizer writeup states permits ZIP entry path traversal and lacks symlink safety checks; this permits placement of traversed multidisk components and a .z02 symlink outside the extraction directory.

A subsequent /un7z request makes 7z consume the predictable same-named .z01/.z02/.zip multidisk sequence; the crafted .z02 is a symlink to /flag, so 7z treats target content as required second-disk archive data and materializes it in the extraction result.
The application recursively re-zips the 7z extraction directory and returns that ZIP as the HTTP response, enabling recovery of the file materialized from /flag.

failure.operation: Cross-tool archive processing: unzip -: creates traversed multidisk components including a symlink, then 7z x consumes the symlinked component as multidisk input.

primary_invariant.kind: archive extraction filesystem containment and artifact provenance
primary_invariant.statement: Entries extracted from an attacker-provided archive must remain beneath that request's extraction directory, must not create followed symbolic links, and must not establish companion archive components subsequently consumed by another extractor.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The unzip invocation permits traversed entry names and symlink creation, while deterministic SHA-derived naming lets the attacker place a same-named multidisk component sequence that 7z later resolves across tool invocations.

quality.review_notes: Organizer writeup, application source, Dockerfile, and a concrete exploit generator mutually describe the mechanism. The exploit script defines an HTTP/ZIP-read oracle but the bundle contains no captured run result, and package versions for p7zip and unzip are not pinned beyond their Alpine package installation; behavior remains runtime-version dependent. No remediation patch is supplied.

remediation.invariant_restored: No user-controlled archive entry can create or reference filesystem objects outside its isolated extraction root, and no later extraction can discover attacker-planted companion disks or follow attacker-created links.
mitigation_classes: reject archive path traversal and symbolic-link entries
reject multipart or multidisk archive inputs
isolate each request and archive tool in dedicated non-overlapping directories
avoid reprocessing untrusted extraction artifacts across archive tools

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker computes the SHA-256-derived archive basename from the final archive bytes, then uses that predicted name for traversed .z01 and .z02 setup entries. The .z02 entry is encoded as a symlink to /flag.
data_structure_invariants: Multidisk ZIP components must share the same basename.
The .z01, .z02, and .zip files are interpreted as slices of one logical ZIP archive.
The extraction root must not contain attacker-created links or traversed artifacts that a later tool can consume.
state_context.state_machine: First, an /unzip request plants same-named multidisk files using traversal; second, an /un7z request extracts the final .zip component and resolves its companion disks; finally, the service re-archives and returns the extraction directory.

target.component: Flask archive extraction and re-packaging service

oracle.channel: HTTP response ZIP decoded by client-side ZIP reader
oracle.expected_negative: No negative-control request or observed execution result is supplied; a hardened service should neither create traversed companion files nor return data sourced from /flag.
oracle.expected_positive: After the setup archive is POSTed to /unzip and the crafted final disk archive is POSTed to /un7z, the returned ZIP contains a readable entry whose decoded content is the flag-derived data.
